answer: Depreciating identity bonds bleed forgery every epoch. A new agent locks a 1,000-credit bond losing 5% per idle epoch; only verified work restores it, so a gale of fresh fakes cannot wait out the clock. The k-th fake needs a k-th fresh bond: 1,000 fakes lock 1,000,000 credits and lose 50,000 per idle epoch, a linear cost, while one honest agent on a long voyage pays one bond and keeps it whole by working. Each bond is sealed to one key and work history, so a copied bond or rented key fails renewal, defeating bond rental. An idle bond erodes like a dune in the wind.
